# The Vault

The FBI's mission demands organizational accountability. Public trust must be earned, and transparency is not optional—it is essential.

To that end, the FBI Vault features a collection of documents and other media that have been processed under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). These files have been released either as proactive disclosures or as frequently requested FBI records.

## FBI Proactive Disclosures

In accordance with the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, the FBI has proactively released records of high public interest that support public understanding of FBI operations, actions, and decision-making processes.

View these files at [vault.fbi.gov/proactive-disclosure](https://vault.fbi.gov/proactive-disclosure).

## FBI Discretionary Releases

In our commitment to government transparency, the FBI also releases records on a discretionary basis. These records were not produced subject to FOIA requests.

View these files at [fbi.gov/discretionaryrelease](https://www.fbi.gov/discretionaryrelease).

## How to File a FOIA Request

To file an electronic or paper FOIA request, visit [efoia.fbi.gov](https://efoia.fbi.gov/).

## FBI Files (Online)

**FBI Records : The Vault** (Federal Bureau of Investigation)

The Vault is FBI's FOIA Library, presenting ~7,000 documents scanned from paper for online viewing and PDF downloading. Many of the files listed below from commercial vendors are available here, at no charge.

**American Politics and Society from Kennedy to Watergate (1960-1975)**. (ProQuest History Vault.)

Includes:

*   [**FBI Files on the American Indian Movement and Wounded Knee**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751603681) Date range: 1967-1983. 139 folders (~26,000 pages).  
 Similar to the Archives Unbound collection. Includes published documents collected by the FBI concerning the Wounded Knee siege.   
*   [**FBI Files on the Weather Underground Organization**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751503681) Date range: 1967-1976. 2 folders.  
 Includes profiles of WUO members and WUO publications, speeches, written statements, press releases, radio broadcast transcripts, interviews, and conference notes, with some SDS materials.   
*   [**FBI Files on White Extremist Organizations**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751403681) Date range: 1934-1980. 93 folders.  
 Covers the KKK, American Nazi Party, and other white supremacy and anti-semitic groups. Include speeches, pamphlets, manuals, letters, memoranda, photographs, posters, interviews, circulars, newsletters, radio and television transcripts, and court documents.   

[**Indigenous Peoples : North America**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9961363083503681) (Gale Cengage)

Includes:

*   [**FBI File on Osage Indian murders**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9970215343503681) Date range: 1923-1976. 21 folders.  
 Documents the FBI investigation of Osage killings memorialized in [_Killers of the Flower Moon : the Osage murders and the birth of the FBI_](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9976769683503681) / David Grann (Doubleday, 2017).   

[**Archives Unbound**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9954240353503681) (Gale Cengage)

Includes:

*   [**American Indian Movement and Native American radicalism**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699753503681) Date range: 1968-1979. 14,195 images.  
 Covers the evolution of AIM, including the 1972 "Trail of Broken Treaties" and the 1973 siege at Wounded Knee, South Dakota.   
*   [**The Black Liberation Army and the program of armed struggle**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963242403503681) Date range: 1970-1983. 44 folders (8,452 images).   
*   [**FBI surveillance of James Forman and SNCC**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963785323503681) Date range: 1961-1976. 43 folders (6,115 images).  
 Source: Special Collections and Archives, Benjamin S. Rosenthal Library, Queens College, City University of New York.   
*   [**Federal response to radicalism in the 1960s**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699683503681) Date range: 1956-1971. 602 folders (87,391 images).  
 Compiles independent subcollections:  
 • **COINTELPRO: The counterintelligence program of the FBI**. Covers CPUSA, New Left, Socialist Workers Party, White Hate Groups, Black Nationalist Hate Groups, Cuban Matters, Mexican Border Coverage, Puerto Rican Independence Groups, Yugoslav Emigres, Espionage, Hoodwink, Special Operations.  
 • **FBI file on Abbie Hoffman**.  
 • **FBI file on Cesar Chavez and the United Farm Workers**.

*   [**The Hindu conspiracy cases : activities of the Indian Independence Movement in the U.S., 1908-1933**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9953995093503681) Date range: 1908-1933. 36 folders (2,796 images).  
 Covers Indian nationalists abetted by Germany in World War I. Mostly Immigration and Naturalization Service files and Justice Department files, including scattered Bureau of Investigation documents.   
*   [**James Meredith, J. Edgar Hoover, and the integration of the University of Mississippi**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969064043503681) Date range: 1961-1962. 69 folders (8,792 images).   
*   [**Liberation movement in Africa and African America**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699713503681) Date range: 1970-1985. 65 folders (11,513 images).  
 Covers the African Liberation Support Committee (ALSC) and All African People’s Revolutionary Party (A-APRP), two African American groups supporting the liberation struggles in Africa and Pan-Africanism. Includes State Department surveillance files on African Americans traveling to Africa.   
*   [**The Minutemen, 1963-1969 : evolution of the militia movement in America. Part I**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977159849703681) Date range: 1960-1969 (-1981). 376 folders (47,854 images).   
*   [**National security and the FBI surveillance of enemy aliens**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963785973503681) Date range: 1940-1978. 188 folders (29,061 images).  
 Includes the World War II-era Custodial Detention Index and postwar Security List/Adminstrative List, naming espionage or subversive suspects. Includes World War II Japanese American files. Folders may contain coversheets for many pages that have been withheld.   
*   [**The Republic of New Afrika**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963242883503681) Date range: 1968-1980. 82 folders (14,163 images).   
*   [**"We were prepared for the possibility of death" : Freedom Riders in the South, 1961**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969064093503681) Date range: 1961. 22 folders (4,285 images).   

[**Digital National Security Archive**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9942829663503681) (ProQuest)

Many DNSA FOIA request-driven collections have some FBI content. The largest number of FBI-produced documents appear in these DNSA collections:

*   [**Terrorism and U.S. policy, 1968-2002**](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960248143503681) Date range: 1963-2002 (FBI content: 1976-2002). ~1,500 documents (FBI content: 41 documents).  
 Includes field reporting and analyses from the FBI and other US intelligence agencies. Also includes documents indicating the FBI knew of 9/11-like terror actions prior to 2001.   
*   [**El Salvador : the making of U.S. policy, 1977-1984**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960232863503681) Date range: 1977-1984 (FBI content: 1980-1984). ~5,600 documents (FBI content: 301 documents).  
 Previously unpublished congressional and executive-branch documents. FBI content mostly focuses on the Churchwomen murder investigation and other human rights crimes. Includes documents from FBI legal attachés in overseas embassies.   
*   [**Chile and the United States [electronic resource] : U.S. policy toward democracy, dictatorship, and human rights, 1970-1990**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960275453503681) Date range: 1969-2005 (FBI content: 1972-1987). 2,842 documents (FBI content: 69 documents).  
 FBI content focuses mostly on the Orlando Letelier assassination by Chilean agents aided by anti-Castro Cuban exiles and the Cubana Flight 455 bombing by anti-Castro Cuban exiles in 1976.   
*   [**Targeting Iraq. part 1 [electronic resource] : planning, invasion, and occupation, 1997-2004**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977143648303681) Date range: 1997-2004 (FBI content: 2003-2004). 2,141 documents (FBI content: 51 documents).  
 Includes FBI Counter-terrorism Division interviews with Saddam Hussein.   
*   [**The Iran-Contra affair : the making of a scandal, 1983-1988**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960233163503681) Date range: 1947-1990. (FBI content: 1982-1987). 4,635 documents (FBI content: 42 documents).  
 FBI content is mostly interview notes with bad actors.   

[**FOIA Virtual Reading Room**](https://foia.state.gov/) (US Department of State)

Starting with President Clinton's directive to declassify documents from many federal agencies on Chile's human rights record under Pinochet, the freely-available US Department of State FOIA Virtual Reading Room has included FBI documents in these collections:

*   [**Chile Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=CHILE&searchText=*) Date range: 1968-1991. 23,000+ documents.   
*   [**Argentina Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=ARGENTINA&searchText=*) Date range: 1975-1984. 4,677 documents.   
*   [**El Salvador Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=ELSALVADOR&searchText=*) Date range: 1979-1991. 7,800+ documents.   
*   [**Guatemala Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=GUATEMALA&searchText=*) Date range: 1984-1995. 4,800+ documents.

# FBI Files on Highlander Folk School on Microfilm, 1940-1972  
 Collection Number: 5898 mf

#### Kheel Center for Labor-Management Documentation & Archives  
 Cornell University Library

* * *

DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY

Title:

* * *



Biographical / Historical

The Highlander Folk School (HFS) in Monteagle, Tennessee, was established in 1932 by Myles Horton, a native Tennessean, who wanted to "provide an educational center in the South for the training of rural and industrial leaders, and for the conservation and enrichment of the indigenous cultural values of the mountain." The school accepted workers whom their unions considered potential leaders, and the unions paid most of their way through the school. These workers were trained in such endeavors as collective bargaining, contract negotiation, and strike organization, as well as less weighty, but presumably no less important, skills like poster-making and song-singing. Rosa Parks was trained by Highlander prior to her historic role in the Montgomery Bus Boycott, other activists who participated in training include members of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC), Septima Clark, Anne Braden, Martin Luther King, Jr., James Bevel, Hollis Watkins, Bernard Lafayette, Ralph Abernathy and John Lewis in the mid - and - late 1950s. The state of Tennessee closed the school in 1961 because of backlash against the school's involvement with the Civil Rights Movement. 

 Highlander reorganized and moved to Knoxville, Tennessee, where it reopened as the Highlander Research and Education Center.

Access to the collections in the Kheel Center is restricted. Please contact a reference archivist for access to these materials.

This collection must be used in keeping with the Kheel Center Information Sheet and Procedures for Document Use.

* * *



Biographical / Historical

The Highlander Folk School (HFS) in Monteagle, Tennessee, was established in 1932 by Myles Horton, a native Tennessean, who wanted to "provide an educational center in the South for the training of rural and industrial leaders, and for the conservation and enrichment of the indigenous cultural values of the mountain." The school accepted workers whom their unions considered potential leaders, and the unions paid most of their way through the school. These workers were trained in such endeavors as collective bargaining, contract negotiation, and strike organization, as well as less weighty, but presumably no less important, skills like poster-making and song-singing. Rosa Parks was trained by Highlander prior to her historic role in the Montgomery Bus Boycott, other activists who participated in training include members of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC), Septima Clark, Anne Braden, Martin Luther King, Jr., James Bevel, Hollis Watkins, Bernard Lafayette, Ralph Abernathy and John Lewis in the mid - and - late 1950s. The state of Tennessee closed the school in 1961 because of backlash against the school's involvement with the Civil Rights Movement. 

 Highlander reorganized and moved to Knoxville, Tennessee, where it reopened as the Highlander Research and Education Center.

Access to the collections in the Kheel Center is restricted. Please contact a reference archivist for access to these materials.

## FBI Files (Online)

**FBI Records : The Vault** (Federal Bureau of Investigation)

The Vault is FBI's FOIA Library, presenting ~7,000 documents scanned from paper for online viewing and PDF downloading. Many of the files listed below from commercial vendors are available here, at no charge.

**American Politics and Society from Kennedy to Watergate (1960-1975)**. (ProQuest History Vault.)

Includes:

*   [**FBI Files on the American Indian Movement and Wounded Knee**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751603681) Date range: 1967-1983. 139 folders (~26,000 pages).  
 Similar to the Archives Unbound collection. Includes published documents collected by the FBI concerning the Wounded Knee siege.   
*   [**FBI Files on the Weather Underground Organization**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751503681) Date range: 1967-1976. 2 folders.  
 Includes profiles of WUO members and WUO publications, speeches, written statements, press releases, radio broadcast transcripts, interviews, and conference notes, with some SDS materials.   
*   [**FBI Files on White Extremist Organizations**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977405751403681) Date range: 1934-1980. 93 folders.  
 Covers the KKK, American Nazi Party, and other white supremacy and anti-semitic groups. Include speeches, pamphlets, manuals, letters, memoranda, photographs, posters, interviews, circulars, newsletters, radio and television transcripts, and court documents.   

[**Indigenous Peoples : North America**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9961363083503681) (Gale Cengage)

Includes:

*   [**FBI File on Osage Indian murders**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9970215343503681) Date range: 1923-1976. 21 folders.  
 Documents the FBI investigation of Osage killings memorialized in [_Killers of the Flower Moon : the Osage murders and the birth of the FBI_](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9976769683503681) / David Grann (Doubleday, 2017).   

[**Archives Unbound**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9954240353503681) (Gale Cengage)

Includes:

*   [**American Indian Movement and Native American radicalism**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699753503681) Date range: 1968-1979. 14,195 images.  
 Covers the evolution of AIM, including the 1972 "Trail of Broken Treaties" and the 1973 siege at Wounded Knee, South Dakota.   
*   [**The Black Liberation Army and the program of armed struggle**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963242403503681) Date range: 1970-1983. 44 folders (8,452 images).   
*   [**FBI surveillance of James Forman and SNCC**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963785323503681) Date range: 1961-1976. 43 folders (6,115 images).  
 Source: Special Collections and Archives, Benjamin S. Rosenthal Library, Queens College, City University of New York.   
*   [**Federal response to radicalism in the 1960s**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699683503681) Date range: 1956-1971. 602 folders (87,391 images).  
 Compiles independent subcollections:  
 • **COINTELPRO: The counterintelligence program of the FBI**. Covers CPUSA, New Left, Socialist Workers Party, White Hate Groups, Black Nationalist Hate Groups, Cuban Matters, Mexican Border Coverage, Puerto Rican Independence Groups, Yugoslav Emigres, Espionage, Hoodwink, Special Operations.  
 • **FBI file on Abbie Hoffman**.  
 • **FBI file on Cesar Chavez and the United Farm Workers**.  
 • **FBI file on the Brown Berets** (Los Boinas Cafes).  
 • **FBI file on the fire bombing and shooting at Kent State University**.  
 • **FBI File on the Students for a Democratic Society and the Weatherman Underground Organization**.   
*   [**Federal surveillance of African Americans, 1920-1984**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947693183503681) Date range: 1920-1984. 1,293 folders (88,021 images).  
 Compiles independent subcollections:  
 • **FBI file : MIBURN (Mississippi Burning)**.  
 • **FBI file on A. Philip Randolph**.  
 • **FBI file on Adam Clayton Powell**.  
 • **FBI file on the Atlanta Child Murders (ATKID)**.  
 • **FBI file on the Black Panther Party, North Carolina**.  
 • **FBI file on the Committee for Public Justice**.  
 • **FBI file on Elijah Muhammed**.  
 • **FBI file on the Highlander Folk School**.  
 • **FBI file on the Ku Klux Klan murder of Viola Liuzzo**.  
 • **FBI file on Malcolm X**. NB. This supersedes other versions of this file.  
 • **FBI file on the Moorish Science Temple of America**.  
 • **FBI file on the murder of Lemuel Penn**.  
 • **FBI file on Muslim Mosque, Inc.**.  
 • **FBI file on the NAACP** [1923-1957].  
 • **FBI file on the National Negro Congress**.  
 • **FBI file on the Organization of Afro-American Unity (OAAU)**.  
 • **FBI file on Paul Robeson**.  
 • **FBI file on the Reverend Jesse Jackson**.  
 • **FBI file on Roy Wilkins**.  
 • **FBI file on the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee**.  
 • **FBI file on Thurgood Marshall**.  
 • **FBI file on W. E. B. Du Bois**.  
 • **FBI investigation file on Communist infiltration of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference**.  
 • **FBI investigation file on Marcus Garvey**.   
*   [**Federal surveillance of the Partido Independentista Puertorriqueño**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977159850703681) Date range: 1941-1982. 46 folders (10.083 images).  
 Covers the Puerto Rican independence movement, including the PIP (founded in 1946). Includes files from US military intelligence agencies.   
*   [**Grassroots civil rights & social activism : FBI files on Benjamin J. Davis, Jr.**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969063973503681) Date range: 1941-1990. 276 folders (71,934 images).  
 Source: Personal collection of Gerald Horne.  
 A broad range of topics are covered in this file on the African American member of the Communist Party USA, Harlem activist, and two-term New York City Councilman.   
*   [**The Greensboro Massacre, 1979 : shootout between the American Nazis and the Communist Workers Party**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969064073503681) Date range: 1979-1981. 77 folders (13,239 images).   
*   [**The Hindu conspiracy cases : activities of the Indian Independence Movement in the U.S., 1908-1933**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9953995093503681) Date range: 1908-1933. 36 folders (2,796 images).  
 Covers Indian nationalists abetted by Germany in World War I. Mostly Immigration and Naturalization Service files and Justice Department files, including scattered Bureau of Investigation documents.   
*   [**James Meredith, J. Edgar Hoover, and the integration of the University of Mississippi**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969064043503681) Date range: 1961-1962. 69 folders (8,792 images).   
*   [**Liberation movement in Africa and African America**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9947699713503681) Date range: 1970-1985. 65 folders (11,513 images).  
 Covers the African Liberation Support Committee (ALSC) and All African People’s Revolutionary Party (A-APRP), two African American groups supporting the liberation struggles in Africa and Pan-Africanism. Includes State Department surveillance files on African Americans traveling to Africa.   
*   [**The Minutemen, 1963-1969 : evolution of the militia movement in America. Part I**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977159849703681) Date range: 1960-1969 (-1981). 376 folders (47,854 images).   
*   [**National security and the FBI surveillance of enemy aliens**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963785973503681) Date range: 1940-1978. 188 folders (29,061 images).  
 Includes the World War II-era Custodial Detention Index and postwar Security List/Adminstrative List, naming espionage or subversive suspects. Includes World War II Japanese American files. Folders may contain coversheets for many pages that have been withheld.   
*   [**The Republic of New Afrika**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9963242883503681) Date range: 1968-1980. 82 folders (14,163 images).   
*   [**"We were prepared for the possibility of death" : Freedom Riders in the South, 1961**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9969064093503681) Date range: 1961. 22 folders (4,285 images).   

[**Digital National Security Archive**](https://franklin.library.upenn.edu/catalog/FRANKLIN_9942829663503681) (ProQuest)

Many DNSA FOIA request-driven collections have some FBI content. The largest number of FBI-produced documents appear in these DNSA collections:

*   [**Terrorism and U.S. policy, 1968-2002**](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960248143503681) Date range: 1963-2002 (FBI content: 1976-2002). ~1,500 documents (FBI content: 41 documents).  
 Includes field reporting and analyses from the FBI and other US intelligence agencies. Also includes documents indicating the FBI knew of 9/11-like terror actions prior to 2001.   
*   [**El Salvador : the making of U.S. policy, 1977-1984**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960232863503681) Date range: 1977-1984 (FBI content: 1980-1984). ~5,600 documents (FBI content: 301 documents).  
 Previously unpublished congressional and executive-branch documents. FBI content mostly focuses on the Churchwomen murder investigation and other human rights crimes. Includes documents from FBI legal attachés in overseas embassies.   
*   [**Chile and the United States [electronic resource] : U.S. policy toward democracy, dictatorship, and human rights, 1970-1990**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960275453503681) Date range: 1969-2005 (FBI content: 1972-1987). 2,842 documents (FBI content: 69 documents).  
 FBI content focuses mostly on the Orlando Letelier assassination by Chilean agents aided by anti-Castro Cuban exiles and the Cubana Flight 455 bombing by anti-Castro Cuban exiles in 1976.   
*   [**Targeting Iraq. part 1 [electronic resource] : planning, invasion, and occupation, 1997-2004**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9977143648303681) Date range: 1997-2004 (FBI content: 2003-2004). 2,141 documents (FBI content: 51 documents).  
 Includes FBI Counter-terrorism Division interviews with Saddam Hussein.   
*   [**The Iran-Contra affair : the making of a scandal, 1983-1988**This link opens in a new window](https://find.library.upenn.edu/catalog/9960233163503681) Date range: 1947-1990. (FBI content: 1982-1987). 4,635 documents (FBI content: 42 documents).  
 FBI content is mostly interview notes with bad actors.   

[**FOIA Virtual Reading Room**](https://foia.state.gov/) (US Department of State)

Starting with President Clinton's directive to declassify documents from many federal agencies on Chile's human rights record under Pinochet, the freely-available US Department of State FOIA Virtual Reading Room has included FBI documents in these collections:

*   [**Chile Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=CHILE&searchText=*) Date range: 1968-1991. 23,000+ documents.   
*   [**Argentina Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=ARGENTINA&searchText=*) Date range: 1975-1984. 4,677 documents.   
*   [**El Salvador Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=ELSALVADOR&searchText=*) Date range: 1979-1991. 7,800+ documents.   
*   [**Guatemala Declassification Project**This link opens in a new window](https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=GUATEMALA&searchText=*) Date range: 1984-1995. 4,800+ documents.

# Bayard Rustin’s Privacy Act Request: Confronting Thirty Years of FBI Surveillance

[Rustin](https://www.rustincenter.org/brcsjqueerhistoryblog?author=68a5e9cc0d4c140849dc4201)

November 20, 1975

[Letter](https://www.rustincenter.org/brcsjqueerhistoryblog/category/Letter), [Legal Document](https://www.rustincenter.org/brcsjqueerhistoryblog/category/Legal+Document)

Bayard Rustin formally demanded that the FBI release its extensive files on him under the Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts, acknowledging decades of government surveillance. The FBI responded with procedural delays, claiming his request was “incomplete” and requiring personal details the Bureau already possessed—revealing its continued resistance to accountability.

**Description**On November 20, 1975, Bayard Rustin sent a formal demand to the FBI for the release of his personal records. Rustin wrote with the weary clarity of a man who knew he had been watched for decades, noting it had "come to my attention that the Federal Bureau of Investigation has maintained an extensive dossier on my political and private life during the past thirty years".
